chips.text: One more freeze in low spots Friday morning

east_texas.headline: Sunny, chilly and breezy for Thanksgiving. One more cold start Friday, then a quick warm-up to near 70 Saturday.
east_texas.summary: Much of the area reached freezing this morning, with Tyler near 33 and rural low spots in the 20s. Today stays sunny with highs in the low 50s and northwest winds of 10 to 20 mph, gusting near 25 this afternoon. Tonight is clear and calm, with lows near 31 in town and the upper 20s in low spots. Friday morning looks like the last freeze for a while. Highs reach the 60s Friday and near 70 Saturday before a cold front Sunday.
east_texas.rain_note: No rain today through Saturday. A few showers are possible east of I-49 early Sunday, but most of the area stays dry and the drought continues. Models show a better rain chance around Dec 3 to 6.

facts.p: Near 31 in town, upper 20s in rural low spots

No notable outages in Smith or nearby counties

panels.title: The first widespread freeze
paras: Clear skies and light winds let temperatures drop to about 33 in Tyler this morning, with rural low spots in the 20s. NWS Shreveport had a Freeze Warning out for Smith County and much of the region until 9 AM.
Friday morning looks similar but a degree or two milder in town. After that, south winds return and lows climb into the 40s and 50s for the weekend.

panels.title: Warm early December, rain chance returns
paras: The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal temperatures for Texas through Dec 9 and leans wetter than normal in the Dec 3 to 9 period. The European and American models both show a rain system around Dec 3 to 6, though they disagree on timing and amounts.
It is still a week or more out, so confidence is moderate. El Niño remains very strong, which tends to favor a more active storm track later in the winter.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Tyler airport observations, PowerOutage.us, Texas A&M Forest Service, Open-Meteo model data (HRRR, NBM, ECMWF, GFS, Canadian).

tables.title: How cold each morning gets
tables.note: In town means Tyler and other built-up areas. Low spots means rural valleys, creek and river bottoms and sandy open fields, which can run 5 to 8 degrees colder on calm, clear nights. Protect tender plants one more night.

nm.headline: Quiet Thanksgiving in the mountains. Strong winds arrive Saturday, and a wetter storm may follow midweek.
nm.summary: Sunny skies and light winds continue today with seasonal temperatures and some high cirrus. Angel Fire dropped to about 13 this morning, and the high valleys stay very cold tonight. Winds pick up Friday afternoon over the central highlands, then a fast-moving system brings strong northwest winds Saturday. NWS Albuquerque says highland gusts could reach 45 to 60 mph and a High Wind Watch may be issued. Another breezy day comes Monday, and a Pacific storm could bring rain and snow to western and central areas around Wednesday.

nm.snow_note: Start-of-day readings for Thursday. Little change in dry weather. Taos Powderhorn is at 130 percent of median snow water and Gallegos Peak is at 100 percent.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu reports 7 inches of new snow in the past week and 15 inches for the season. Resort base depths include man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Strong winds over the highlands
paras: A fast-moving system dives out of the northern Rockies Saturday. NWS Albuquerque expects the strongest winds near and just east of the central mountain chain in the afternoon, with gusts of 45 to 60 mph possible.

Winds like that can make driving difficult for high-profile vehicles and can damage weak trees and utility poles. Winds ease in the west Saturday evening but stay strong in the northeast past midnight.

panels.title: Icy stretch still listed on US-64
paras: NMRoads still lists US-64 east of Taos (mile markers 257 to 272) as snow packed and icy, last updated Tuesday. No severe driving conditions are listed anywhere in the state.
Nothing is listed for the interstates or for NM-518, NM-434, NM-38, NM-75, NM-150 or NM-68.

panels.title: Wetter pattern next week
paras: NWS Albuquerque says a deeper Pacific low could bring rain and snow to parts of western and central New Mexico around Wednesday.

The Climate Prediction Center favors wetter than normal conditions around the Four Corners Dec 3 to 9. El Niño is very strong, which tends to favor better snow odds in northern New Mexico as winter goes on.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, Angel Fire airport observations, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, Sipapu snow report, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
